name: Spot (Irish Rummy)
description: Spot is a traditional Irish rummy game for 4 players, played for small stakes in pubs and homes. It uses an 8-card hand and a standard 52-card deck (Ac-10-K-Q-J-9 is NOT used, standard A=1, 2-10, J-K=10). The goal is to 'Drop' melds (sets of 3+ or sequences of 3+) to reduce the spot value of remaining cards. A player cannot drop more than 4 cards at once.

history.origins: Spot is a rummy game from the west of Ireland, played for small stakes in pubs and private houses. Its name comes from the spot values of cards (A=1, 2–10 face value, J/Q/K=10) used to settle payments at the end of each hand. It is likely a local variant of Basic Rummy or 500 Rummy, with the distinctive rule that no player may drop more than four cards in one turn. Traditionally stakes were a penny per spot with a 5-unit ante before the introduction of the Euro.
timeline: 1980s: Still common in Galway and Mayo.
history.cultural: Often played for pennies per spot.
history.evolution: The 4-card drop limit is a unique anti-sandbagging rule.

setup.players: Usually 4; same rules allow more or fewer.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack, no jokers; Aces low.
setup.dealing: Ante to pot. Deal 8 cards each. 9th card to player left of dealer (start).
setup.equipment: Agreed stake (traditionally 1 unit per spot, 5-unit ante).

rules.objective: Go out (Shed all cards) or have lowest spot count.
rules.gameplay: Each turn: draw one card from stock or top of discard pile; optionally drop up to four cards as new groups or runs or add to existing table melds (groups of 3–4 equal rank, runs of 3+ same suit, Aces low); discard one card face up. First player does not draw, only drops and discards. No player may drop more than four cards in one turn. Play ends when a player goes out by discarding their last card, or when stock is exhausted.
keyRules: Max four cards may be dropped in one turn; only one new group or run per turn.
Aces are always low; Q-K-A is not a valid run.
Going out requires a final discard; a player with two cards who draws a completing card must discard one and cannot go out that turn.

strategy.basic: Form melds quickly. Don't hold high cards (K, Q, J) hoping for a meld unless you have two. Discard 10-pointers early if unmatching.
strategy.intermediate: The 4-Card Limit: You can't drop a 5-card run (e.g., 3-4-5-6-7) in one go. You must drop 3-4-5-6, then add 7 next turn? No, add to existing melds later. Plan your drops.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: Don't give the next player a card they need to go out. If they pick up a 7, don't throw an 8 or 6.
tips: The pot can grow large with antes.
